content: 1. Comparisons that are statistically differentiable are indicated in bold. 2. The values for LPV/r represent the effect of the treatment in the row relative to the treatment in the column. 3. Odds ratios greater than 1 suggest higher rates of treatment-emergent adverse events of all causes. 4. Bold values highlight comparisons that are statistically significant. 5. The values for NVP represent the effect of the treatment lower on the diagonal compared to the one higher on it. 6. Odds ratios above 1 indicate greater efficacy in achieving viral suppression. 7. EFV refers to efavirenz, NVP to nevirapine, RAL 400 to raltegravir 400 mg, RAL 800 to raltegravir 800 mg, and LPV/r to ritonavir-boosted lopinavir. 8. The GRADE summary tables provide evidence quality assessments for children and adolescents. 9. Direct estimates are derived from available direct evidence, while indirect estimates are based on network meta-analysis (NMA) when direct evidence is unavailable. 10. Combined estimates are NMA-derived for comparisons where direct evidence exists. 11. Uncombined estimates start with high-quality evidence and are adjusted based on factors like precision and consistency. 12. The quality of evidence can be upgraded if penalties for precision in uncombined scores are resolved in network estimates. 13. Consistency was evaluated using I² statistics and visual inspection of point estimates. An I² value of 75% or higher indicates significant heterogeneity. 14. Risk of bias was downgraded if most studies in a comparison were at high risk of bias, both for direct and indirect pathways. 15. Indirectness was downgraded when estimates relied solely on indirect evidence. 16. The GRADE framework assesses the quality of evidence and strength of recommendations, considering factors like imprecision, inconsistency, and publication bias. 17. Viral suppression rates are reported per 1,000 individuals, with varying levels of evidence quality (low, moderate, or very low). 18. The final quality of evidence reflects updates from uncombined evidence, with adjustments for precision and transitivity violations. 19. References include key WHO guidelines, systematic reviews, and GRADE methodology papers.
